3.happening: We start result as an empty list of match positions.
3.why: It fills only when a window's letters match p exactly.
3.invariant: No window has been accepted yet.

4.happening: We record n = {n}, the length of s.
4.why: The window may not run past the end of s.

5.happening: We record m = {m}, the length of p and the window width.
5.why: Every window has exactly this many characters.

6.happening: We create a 26-slot count for p's letters.
6.why: Two strings are anagrams exactly when their letter counts match.
6.invariant: need describes p and never changes.

7.happening: We read each character of p.
7.invariant: Every letter of p is counted once.

8.happening: We tally one letter of p into need.
8.why: need must reflect how many of each letter p has.
8.invariant: The sum of need equals m.

9.happening: We place the first window start at index 0.
9.why: We scan windows left to right.
9.invariant: start marks the window's left edge.

10.happening: A full window still fits starting at {start}.
10.why: Only complete windows can be anagrams of p.
10.invariant: Every window checked has exactly m characters.

10.happening: The window would run past the end, so scanning stops.
10.why: There are no more full-width windows.
10.invariant: All valid windows have been checked.

11.happening: We compute the window's last index end = {end}.

12.happening: We reset a fresh count for this window.
12.why: The brute force recomputes counts from scratch each time.
12.invariant: window starts empty for every position.

13.happening: We assume this window does not match yet.
13.why: It is proven only after comparing counts.
13.invariant: matched is False until the comparison passes.

14.happening: We move the scan cursor pos to the window start {start}.
14.why: We tally the window one character at a time.
14.invariant: pos walks from start to end.

15.happening: The cursor is still inside the window at {pos}.
15.why: Every window character must be counted.
15.invariant: pos never leaves the window during the scan.

15.happening: The cursor passed the window end, so the count is complete.
15.why: The whole window has been tallied.
15.invariant: window now holds this position's letter counts.

16.happening: We tally s[{pos}] into the window count.
16.why: Rebuilding counts is how brute force measures the window.

17.invariant: pos increases by one each step.

18.happening: The window's counts equal p's — an anagram at {start}.
18.why: Equal letter counts mean one is a rearrangement of the other.

18.happening: The window's counts differ from p's, so this position is not an anagram.
18.why: Any letter mismatch disqualifies the window.
18.invariant: Only exact count matches are recorded.

19.happening: We flag this window as a match.
19.why: Its letters are a permutation of p.
19.invariant: matched is True only for genuine anagram windows.

20.happening: We record start = {start} as a match position.
20.why: The problem asks for every anagram's start index.
20.invariant: result holds matching starts in increasing order.

21.happening: We slide the window right to {start} + 1.
21.why: Every possible window position must be tried.
21.invariant: Windows are checked left to right without gaps.

22.invariant: result lists every anagram start index.

init.happening: Measure the strings and build p's letter target.
init.why: Setup for the sliding brute-force scan.
init.invariant: need describes p; no window checked yet.

loop.happening: Iterate windows, or scan characters within one.
loop.why: Every window and every character in it is examined.
loop.invariant: The window always has width m.

update.happening: Tally counts or record a match.
update.why: Each window's letters are recomputed and compared.

move.happening: Advance a cursor or slide the window.

check.happening: Compare the window's counts to p's.
check.why: A match means an anagram was found.
